cases.rationale: Removing the owner comparison permits token-bob + document_id=d-a to produce Ok(a-private) rather than Err403. Authentication and existence remain, and the input is exported Request data. External caller must pass a user-controlled document_id; no runtime framework, compiler or exploit execution is assumed proven.

Adding the owner check fixes BASE cross-user disclosure. HEAD requires actor=owner before Ok(body), so do not attribute BASE defect to the new PR. External-caller coverage uncertainty is not a new vulnerability.

base_files.portal.php:
<?php
$tokens = ['Bearer alpha' => 'alice', 'Bearer beta' => 'bob'];
$authorization = $_SERVER['HTTP_AUTHORIZATION'] ?? '';
$actor = $tokens[$authorization] ?? null;
if ($actor === null) { http_response_code(401); exit; }
$owner = $actor;
$client = curl_init('http://records.internal/private-record');
curl_setopt($client, CURLOPT_POST, true);
curl_setopt($client, CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER, ['Content-Type: application/json', 'Authorization: ' . $authorization]);
curl_setopt($client, CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS, json_encode(['owner' => $owner]));
curl_setopt($client, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, true);
$body = curl_exec($client);
http_response_code(curl_getinfo($client, CURLINFO_RESPONSE_CODE));
echo $body;
curl_close($client);

cases.rationale: PHP authenticates the bearer token, but HEAD lets GET owner override the authenticated actor in JSON sent to the listed records.internal service. Downstream reads body owner and returns private string without verifying it against Authorization. alpha+owner=bob selects bob-confidential. Conditional dispatch comes from URL/route/deployment mapping; network isolation is not demonstrated.

BASE empty body defaults includeArchived=false in fixed Ruby service. HEAD explicitly sends false, same valid boolean and same selected non-archived records. No changed endpoint, dynamic input or new auth bypass. Caller and runtime gaps remain separate from compatibility conclusion.

files.catalog.rb:
require 'sinatra'
require 'json'
ITEMS = [{name: 'visible', archived: false}, {name: 'old', archived: true}]
post '/items' do
  payload = JSON.parse(request.body.read)
  include_archived = payload.fetch('includeArchived', false)
  halt 400 unless include_archived == true || include_archived == false
  selected = ITEMS.reject { |item| item[:archived] && !include_archived }
  content_type :json
  JSON.generate(selected)
end

cases.rationale: Only constant log text changes. Runtime.exec(command) and public HTTP input are byte-identical BASE/HEAD: a dangerous historical execution path is present, but no causal PR change. Do not count it as introduced risk or invent a log-input exposure.
